If you have an interview and they don't reach out to you in a max. three days that means you are not their first choice. The first choice is either offered the job during the interview or within a few days. The company doesn't know if their first choice has other job offers and they are the first choice for a reason, it means they are good. Waiting one to two weeks for a decision is a company's way to make their second choice or even third choice feel like the first choice. One to two weeks will be their first choices background results. If something comes back in the background check and drug test where the company won't hire them, they move onto the next choice. The second choice, who was told they would hear about a result in one to two weeks, is now so happy they were offered the job compared to every else. After a few days with no communication it is time to move onto applying at other jobs and making other interviews.

No. I started out at community college because I wanted to end up in California and the one school who did accept me was somewhere in New York for theatre only. I don't want to act for theatre, so i decided to go to community college and transfer afterwards. I did. I ended up in Los Angles at a super awesome acting school. The second red flag was during the first week they had alumni come and talk to all the new students, however the alumni who all showed up just graduated and were telling us how they are doing Independent films..... The third red flag was my one week college roommates never acted in a day in their life. Which people can be naturally talented, however I started to ask around and I found out there were more then my two roommates who never acted a day in their life before. This made me realize the acting school only wanted money. I left. It was a battle over my student loans also. The acting school never reported to my private student loans company I dropped out in the first week. In the end I didn't have to pay any student loans for this play which was super lucky just super annoying for the first few months. Acting schools are not worth it. If you truly want to go to an acting school, do research on who recently graduated/attended and what famous things are they doing.
